text:
incident-bot: PAGER: High latency spike detected for /v1/generate (alert: core-inference-latency). Incident link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-0422
Alex: grabbing this as I'm starting my shift now — I'll be primary driver. quick status?
Jamie: hey Alex — we're ~5m into the spike, p90 for token generation jumped from 200ms to ~2.1s. errors are 0.5% but users hitting timeouts in a couple of regions.
Samir: assigning comms to Samir now. I'll stay as secondary for 20m while I finish the handoff.
Alex: @Samir you're comms. I'll take driver. Jamie — any active mitigations already?
Jamie: yes, automated fallback routing kicked in to model-small in eu-west, which reduced errors but increased latency overall due to cross-region routing. We also started a rolling restart on one pod group that had degraded metrics.
Samir: copying customers list -> affected: a subset of hosted-api customers in eu-west (IDs redwood-cust-11, redwood-cust-21). I'll draft initial comms: "We are investigating increased generation latency; no data loss. More updates in 15m."
Alex: runbook pointer: https://redwood.runbooks/latency-spike - follow section "Immediate mitigations". First step: check model-serving queue depth and KV-cache pressure.
Jamie: stack trace shows KV cache misses trending up. Probe command I ran:```bash
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=model-server -o wide
kubectl -n inference exec -it model-server-5 -- curl localhost:8080/metrics | grep kv_cache_miss
```
Alex: good. I'm going to scale up the model-server pool by +2 replicas in eu-west and disable cross-region fallback for write-heavy routes to avoid extra RTT. Command:```bash
# scale
kubectl -n inference scale deploy/model-server-eu --replicas=6
# disable fallback route (temporary)
redwoodctl routing update --route-host=api-host --disable-cross-region-fallback
```
Samir: noted. I'll post an interim update to status page and ping support. Draft: "Investigation underway; scaling servers and adjusting routing. Expected update within 15 minutes." :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Megan: I'm on phone but reachable. If this persists past 20m I can jump in.
Jamie: small gap: my next shift start overlaps by 5 minutes where I'll be offline for a quick call. Alex, do you want me to remain secondary until Megan is fully available?
Alex: yes please remain secondary for the next 15m. Samir — if anything customer-facing changes, coordinate with Jamie for technical detail before posting.
Samir: will do. Creating a short bulletin now.
incident-bot: NOTE: Pager escalations remain enabled. Next on-call escalation: Megan at 1735013600.
Alex: timeline check — plan: immediate scale + routing toggle (5-10m), observe metrics for 10m, if p95 > 1s then failover to smaller model pool for affected customers (use rollout key "fallback-model-small").
Jamie: adding rollback play if scale doesn't help: revert routing toggle and roll a controlled restart of model-shard-3 only.
Samir: posted initial status update to status.redwood.com/incidents/1735012345 — linking here. I'll update again in 12 minutes.
Alex: ok team — primary driver = Alex, comms = Samir, secondary = Jamie for 15m, backup = Megan after that. No coverage gaps expected but flagging the 5m window Jamie mentioned. If that window bites, Samir you may need to call Megan.
Samir: acknowledged.
Alex: starting mitigation now. I'll post a final summary once we've stabilized or hit next escalation. :clipboard:
